newsitem.title: UK: UK's Ashdown says does not favour pact with Labour.
newsitem.headline: UK's Ashdown says does not favour pact with Labour.

text.p: Paddy Ashdown, leader of Britain's minority Liberal Democrats, said on Tuesday he was opposed to a post-election pact in which his party would help to prop up a Labour government.
"I'm not in favour of pacts. The party's not in favour of them," Ashdown told Britain's Press Association agency in an interview.
"I'm in favour of working sensibly with other parties on things we agree on," he added.
The latest national opinion poll gave the Liberals just 13 percent support, with Labour 18 points ahead of the Conservatives.
Unless Labour support falls sharply in the run-up to an election now expected on May 1, its leader Tony Blair will not need Liberal support to govern. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
